t: You're on Great Newport Street, a street in the City of Westminster. It takes its name from Mountjoy Blount, the first Earl of Newport, an English courtier and politician who served Charles I as Master of the Ordnance and backed the Royalists in the First English Civil War. The street is also where the embroiderer and designer Phoebe Wright died, in 1778. She founded and ran what she called the Royal School of embroidering females, so a quiet piece of London's needlework history ends here.
